title: NEMAR Zarr serving index (format_version 3)
description: The mandatory entry point to a dataset's Zarr serving copy at <data_base>index.json. Anonymous ListBucket is denied on the serving bucket, so this document -- not a listing -- is how a client discovers what is served, where to read it from, and why a recording is missing. Produced by scripts/zarr/generate_zarr.py (nemarOrg/nemar-cli); consumed by nemar.org, the backend catalog sweep, and external clients. contract_base is the only URL a client may hardcode: data_base / s3_uri describe where the bytes happen to live today and may change per dataset.

contract_base.description: The STABLE base URL for this dataset's serving copy (https://<zarr host>/<id>/zarr/). The only base a client may hardcode.

data_base.description: Where the bytes are served from TODAY, for an HTTP Zarr reader. May change; re-read it from this document rather than hardcoding it.

data_base_kind.description: What kind of thing data_base points at, so a client knows which access pattern applies.

s3_uri.description: The same location as an s3:// triple, for boto3 / s3fs / zarr, which want bucket+key rather than a URL to parse back apart.

s3_anonymous.description: True when s3_uri is readable with unsigned requests (no credentials needed).

source_commit.description: The dataset repository commit this serving copy was built from. Always a full 40-hex SHA; the producer refuses to publish an index without one (#1197).

engine_version.description: The discovery/dispatch generation that produced this index (zarr_queue.ZARR_ENGINE_VERSION). Changes only when discovery widens; see ADR 0033.

biosigio_version.description: The biosigIO release that wrote the stores, or null when it could not be determined.

updated_utc.description: When this run wrote the index (UTC, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).

discovered_count.description: Raw recordings the walker found at source_commit, after the ADR 0027 exclusions (derivatives/, sourcedata/, code/, BIDS MEG calibration files). The denominator of coverage. INVARIANT: discovered_count == store_count + failure_count + pending_count.

store_count.description: Recordings with a served store. Authoritative -- prefer it to stores.length.

n_recordings.description: Alias of store_count, kept for the #1059 field list. Not the discovered total; that is discovered_count.

errors.description: Recordings that failed in THIS run, typed and untyped alike. A run statistic, not a coverage total: the coverage totals are failure_count and pending_count, which carry across runs.

failure_count.description: Entries in failures[] -- recordings that will not convert without a change to the data or the converter.

pending_count.description: Entries in pending[] -- recordings with no store yet that are still expected to convert on a later run.

store.description: One converted recording. Read the bytes at <contract_base><zarr>/.

path.description: The recording's path inside the BIDS dataset, relative to the repository root.

zarr.description: The store's path relative to contract_base / data_base.

source_tree.description: Which BIDS tree the SOURCE recording lives in. Always 'raw' for anything converted since ADR 0027; the other values exist only for stores published before it.

derived.description: True when the served signal is PROCESSED rather than the source signal quantised and rate-capped. Today the only true case is an ADR 0028 Signal-Space Separation MEG store, which also carries `sss`. Deliberately distinct from source_tree, which is about BIDS layout.

n_events.description: Rows in the events.tsv the converter applied. Absent when the recording has no applicable events.tsv (which is not the same as an empty one).

trial_types.description: Counts per trial_type value in that same events.tsv, so a client can pick an epoching strategy without reading a signal byte. Absent when there is no events.tsv; an empty object means the file has no trial_type column.

units_report.description: biosigIO's per-file account of what the BIDS channels.tsv `units` column did (biosigio#125), republished so a unit that could NOT be adopted is visible without opening the store. Absent when no channels.tsv was applied to the recording -- either the dataset ships none that inherits to it, or the sidecar could not be read. Never means "applied cleanly". Both the in-memory and the streaming exporter apply it (biosigio>=1.2.7), so the two cannot disagree about a recording's units.

sidecar.description: Repository-relative path of the channels.tsv the converter resolved (BIDS inheritance: the most specific applicable sidecar, which may live in an ancestor directory).

sidecar_supplied.description: True when the converter passed that sidecar to the exporter explicitly rather than relying on sibling auto-detection. Load-bearing for the ADR 0028 MaxShield path, where the exporter is handed a filtered copy in a scratch directory with no sidecar beside it.

split_members.description: Every source path of a split FIF chain served by this one store, so a click on split-02 resolves here.

sss.description: ADR 0028 Signal-Space Separation parameters, present exactly when derived is true.

group.description: One channel group inside a store (biosigIO names them <modality>_<rate>hz). Groups are concurrent streams of ONE recording: a store's duration is the max over its groups, never their sum.

rate.description: The SERVING rate after the NEMAR modality cap, not the acquisition rate. The acquisition rate is source_rate_hz (and the BIDS sidecar's SamplingFrequency).

source_rate_hz.description: The recording's own sampling rate before the cap (level-0 attr).

n_view_levels.description: How many view/* min-max envelope levels exist, so a reader never probes for them (#1178 item 2).

view_chunk_columns.description: Columns per view chunk -- constant across levels since biosigio 1.2.6, so a viewport-sized read is 1-3 requests at any level (#1178 item 1).

failure.description: A recording that has no store for a reason retrying will not change: a property of the data, or a converter gap someone has to close.

code.description: Stable machine code (biosigIO's own, plus the NEMAR-side recording_too_large / channel_count_mismatch / maxshield_uncalibrated / retry_exhausted).

reason.description: The sanitized, user-facing sentence the viewer shows. Never a raw exception.

detail.description: Operator-facing cause: the exception class plus the first line of its message, with local filesystem paths stripped. This is what makes an opaque file_read_error diagnosable from the public index (#1197).

pending.description: A discovered recording with no store yet that is still expected to convert. Recorded rather than omitted so every raw recording is accounted for: before v3 these were silently absent from stores AND failures, which from outside is indistinguishable from 'still generating' forever (#1197).

reason.description: infra_failure: an untyped error (crashed worker, transient S3). memory_budget: it did not fit the memory free on the node at the time, which is a condition, not a property of the recording. not_attempted: this run did not reach it.

attempts.description: Conversion attempts so far. At 5 the producer promotes the entry to a failures[] entry with code retry_exhausted, so a permanently failing recording stops consuming the queue.
